title: Introduce atomic surface steps and shadow micro-ramp for dense components
creator: Lena Park
description:
Background: our existing elevation and surface tokens are coarse (flat/raised/deep) which causes visual inconsistency in dense UI (tables, compact lists, small chips) and makes subtle focus/hover states feel either too pronounced or invisible. This ticket proposes a small, tightly scoped token update: an atomic surface step system (micro surface steps) and a shadow micro-ramp that provides 4–6 finely graduated elevation levels intended specifically for compact components and high-density layouts.

Goals:
- Provide 4 micro elevation tokens (surface-01 .. surface-04) + matching shadow ramps suitable for 8px/touch and 4px/dense spacing contexts.
- Keep a simple migration path from existing tokens; avoid breaking default component look for non-dense modes.
- Maintain or improve contrast/accessibility for focus and active states in both light and dark modes.
- Expose CSS variable naming that is intuitive for engineers and maps to Figma tokens.

Scope: tokens (color overlays, elevation shadows), token naming conventions, updated token docs, Figma components for tables/buttons/chips, a minimal migration guide for component library, and visual regression tests. Not included: full redesign of all components or behavior changes to motion/animation beyond shadow alpha changes.
acceptance_criteria: Four new micro surface tokens (micro-surface-01..04) and four matching shadow definitions exist in the tokens registry and are available as CSS variables.
Figma styles and components are updated: table rows (compact mode), small buttons, input fields, and chips render correctly against the new micro surface tokens.
Migration guide added to the tokens docs with examples: how to map old elevation tokens to micro steps, and a suggested fallback strategy.
Automated visual regression suite covers dense table + small-button states (idle, hover, focus, pressed) with baseline screenshots added to CI.
Engineering sign-off: ENG-2812 implements CSS variables and confirms performance impact is negligible; PR linked.
Accessibility check: contrast of highlighted row and focus ring against micro-surface tokens meets WCAG 2.1 AA for text and interactive targets where applicable.
decisions: Adopt a neutral naming convention: --rdw-surface-micro-01 .. --rdw-surface-micro-04 to distinguish from existing surface tokens.

Shadow ramp will use three-layered shadows (soft ambient + directional + rim) but with reduced blur and alpha to keep density light; values will be parameterized by token rather than hardcoded in components.
Color overlay approach for raised surfaces will prefer a single tone overlay color with variable alpha instead of separate color tokens per elevation to reduce combinatorial explosion.
Default for non-dense components remains unchanged; components gain an opt-in `data-density="micro"` attribute for applying micro tokens.
Figma file will carry both the new micro tokens and a migration sheet showing mapping and visual examples (compact table vs classic table).
notes: We intentionally limit to 4 micro steps after reviewing product needs — more steps increased cognitive overhead without clear benefit.
Shadow values tuned against 12px baseline on desktop and 8px baseline on compact mobile; engineering to expose token scales for breakpoints.
Be mindful of additive shadows when stacking components (floating menu above a micro-surface) — engineering should ensure z-index stacking uses composited shadow isolation where possible.
Consider exposing a token `--rdw-elevation-blend-mode` for future experiments with subtle overlay blend modes in dark mode.
Will record a short Loom demonstrating Figma changes for front-end engineers to reduce hand-off friction.
visual_regression_tests: Add CI job: visual-regression:compact-density that runs screenshots for table/button/chip permutations.
Baseline images collected from Chrome desktop 136 at 1440x900; future runs compare per-pixel diffs and highlight >2% changes.
Include small-device mobile baseline for 375px width with 2x DPR for compact controls.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Design): finalize token numeric values and Figma components — complete by 2026-03-04.
Phase 2 (Engineering): expose CSS variables and add data-density prop to components; land feature flag behind `micro-surface`; expected PR target 2 weeks after Phase 1.

Phase 3 (Rollout): default off for existing pages; opt-in on selected product routes for internal dogfooding. Collect metrics (render diffs, user-reported visual regressions) for two sprints before enabling more broadly.
Phase 4 (Docs): publish migration guide and update component docs with example code snippets and Figma links.
